In the name of God Amen. I Jesse Dean, colored man, of Little Creek Hundred, Kent Co. and the state of Delaware being weak and sick of body but sound and disposing mind and memory do make and ordain this as and for my last will and testament in writing hereby revoking and making void all former wills by me at anytime heretofore made. And first I direct that my body shall be buried in a decent and Christialike manner and I assign my Soul to the keeping of Almighty God and as it respects such real and personal estate as I am the owner of I hereby dispose of the same in the manner following that is to say. Secondly I give and devise unto my son William Dean of Duck Creek Hundred in the County aforesaid and to his heirs and assigns forever, all of my land and real estate with the building, improvements and appertenances situate, lying and being on the east side of the main state road leading from Dover to Smyrna in the county aforesaid and which is part of the tract upon which I now reside and contains about five acres more or less. Thirdly, I give and devise unto my son Jesse Dean of Little Creek Hundred in the county aforesaid and to his heirs and assigns forever, all my land and real estate with the buildings, improvements and appertenances situate, lying or being on the west side of the main state road leading from Dover to Smyrna in the county aforesaid and which conatins about fifteen acres more or less. Fourthly I give and bequeath unto my said son William Dean one calf now about six months old and one hog now in the pen and my colt. Fifthly, I give and bequeath unto my said son Jesse Dean two hogs now in the pen, my bay horse, horse cart and harness, one brindle and pied cow and her calf not yet weaned, said cow being no horned and one small young steer about eighteen months old, the large stove and the piece of carpeting which now hangs at the foot of my bed. Sixthly, I give and bequeath unto Elisha Durham , colored man, his executors, administrators and assigns the bed, bedstead and its furniture upon which I now lie, the bureau at the head of the said bed, the large rush bottomed arm chair, and the six yellow wooden bottomed chairs, the carpet now on the floor, my best cow, two hogs now in the pen, one red and white cow with long slim horns and her calf, and one small candle stand, upon the trust following, that is to say, Upon Trust to permit and suffer my daughter Sally Ann the wife of a certaine John Cott to have the use, possession, disposal and enjoyment of the same, so that the same or any part or parcel thereof shall not be liable for the debts, engagements or liabilities of her said husband the said John Cott. Seventhly, I give and bequeath unto my granddaughter Mary , the legacy or sum of two dollars to be paid to her by my executor within one month from the time of my decease; and I give to Elijah Concealor the pieced bed quilt upstairs which was made by his mother my last wife. Eighthly And as to the rest, residue and remainder of my real and personal estate not hereuntofore specifically disposed of, it is my will and desire that the same shall be sold by my Executor herein named and the proceeds thereof applied in the first place to the payment of my debts and funeral expenses and the remainder after payment thereof to be paid over to my three children above named in the following manner, that is to say, two fifths parts thereof to be paid into the hands of my said daughter, Sally Ann and the balance or other three fifths thereof to be divided amond and paid unto my two abovenamed sons in equal share and proportions. Ninthly, I do hereby except out of the sale of the residue of my property, my hay, husks and fodder, and I direct that the same shall be fed away upon the land to the stock herein before disposed of to my said children, so that the land and (unclear) as the said stock may receive benefit thereof, and I do hereby further except out of the sale of the said residue, the buckwheat which I now have and my old silver watch and I direct that my son Jesse shall have two bushels of said buckwheat and the residue if any together with the said watch shall be delivered to my said daughter, Sally Ann; and I also further except out of the sale of the said residue my wheat (fan?) and I direct that the said shall be delivered to my son William. And whereas my two above named children, William and Jesse, are not legitimate but were born before my intermarriage with their mother Rebecca , now I do hereby adopt the said William and Jesse as my sons,and designate them as the persons above named as susch. Lastly, I do hereby nominate, constitute and appoint the before named Elisha Durham as the Executor of this my last will and testament. (5 line unreadable...crossed out) Signed in Jesse's hand & sealed The State of Delaware Kent County, SS James Farrow one of the subscribing witnesses to the foregoing instrument of writing purporting to be the Last will and Testament of Jesse Dean late of Little Creek Hundred dec'd Comes before (unclear) Register for the Probate of wills and being sworn deposeth and said that he saw the said Jesse Dean the Testator, sign the said Instrument and saw him also seal the same and heard him publish pronounce and declare the same as (unclear) his last will & Testament that at the time of his so doing he was of souund & disposing mind and memory and upward of 20 years of age. That the deponent attested and subscribed his name as a witness to the said Instrument of writing at the Instance and in the presence of the said jesse Dean the Testator and in the presence of the oath witness. (signed) james S. Probate-Jesse Dean

In the name of God Amen. I Jesse Dean, colored man, of Little Creek Hundred, Kent  Co. 
and the state of Delaware being weak and sick of body but sound and disposing mind and memory 
do make and ordain this as and for my last will and testament in writing hereby revoking 
and making void all former wills by me at anytime heretofore made. 

And first I direct that my body shall be buried in a decent and Christialike manner 
and I assign my Soul to the keeping of Almighty God and as it respects such real and 
personal estate as I am the owner of I hereby dispose of the same in the manner following that is to say. 

Secondly I give and devise unto my son  William Dean  of Duck Creek Hundred in the 
County aforesaid and to his heirs and assigns forever, all of my land and real estate 
with the building, improvements and appertenances situate, lying and being on the east 
side of the main state road leading from Dover to Smyrna in the county aforesaid and which 
is part of the tract upon which I now reside and contains about five acres more or less. 

Thirdly, I give and devise unto my son  Jesse Dean  of Little Creek Hundred in the 
county aforesaid and to his heirs and assigns forever, all my land and real estate with 
the buildings, improvements and appertenances situate, lying or being on the west side of the 
main state road leading from Dover to Smyrna in the county aforesaid and which conatins about 
fifteen acres more or less. 

Fourthly I give and bequeath unto my said son William Dean one calf now about six months old 
and one hog now in the pen and my colt. 

Fifthly, I give and bequeath unto my said son Jesse Dean two hogs now in the pen, my bay 
horse, horse cart and harness, one brindle and pied cow and her calf not yet weaned, said 
cow being no horned and one small young steer about eighteen months old, the large stove 
and the piece of carpeting which now hangs at the foot of my bed. 

Sixthly, I give and bequeath unto  Elisha Durham , colored man, his executors, 
administrators and assigns the bed, bedstead and its furniture upon which I now lie, 
the bureau at the head of the said bed, the large rush bottomed arm chair, and the six 
yellow wooden bottomed chairs, the carpet now on the floor, my best cow, two hogs now in 
the pen, one red and white cow with long slim horns and her calf, and one small candle 
stand, upon the trust following, that is to say, Upon Trust to permit and suffer 
my daughter Sally Ann the wife of a certaine  John Cott to have the use, 
possession, disposal and enjoyment of the same, so that the same or any part or parcel 
thereof shall not be liable for the debts, engagements or liabilities of her said husband 
the said John Cott. 

Seventhly, I give and bequeath unto my granddaughter  Mary , the legacy 
or sum of two dollars to be paid to her by my executor within one month from 
the time of my decease; and I give to  Elijah Concealor  the pieced bed quilt 
upstairs which was made by his mother my last wife. 

Eighthly And as to the rest, residue and remainder of my real and personal estate not 
hereuntofore specifically disposed of, it is my will and desire that the same shall be 
sold by my Executor herein named and the proceeds thereof applied in the first place to 
the payment of my debts and funeral expenses and the remainder after payment thereof to 
be paid over to my three children above named in the following manner, that is to say, 
two fifths parts thereof to be paid into the hands of my said daughter, Sally Ann and the 
balance  or other three fifths thereof to be divided amond and paid unto my two abovenamed 
sons in equal share and proportions. 

Ninthly, I do hereby except out of the sale of the residue of my property, my hay, husks 
and fodder, and I direct that the same shall be fed away upon the land to the stock herein 
before disposed of to my said children, so that the land and (unclear) as the said stock may 
receive benefit thereof, and I do hereby further except out of the sale of the said residue, 
the buckwheat which I now have and my old silver watch and I direct that my son Jesse shall 
have two bushels of said buckwheat and the residue if any together with the said watch shall
 be delivered to my said daughter, Sally Ann; and I also further except out of the sale of the 
said residue my wheat (fan?) and I direct that the said shall be delivered to my son William. 

And whereas my two above named children, William and Jesse, are not legitimate but were born 
before my intermarriage with their mother  Rebecca , now I do hereby adopt the said 
William and Jesse as my sons,and designate them as the persons above named as susch. 

Lastly, I do hereby nominate, constitute and appoint the before named Elisha Durham as the Executor    
of this my last will and testament. 

(5 line unreadable...crossed out) 

Signed in Jesse's hand & sealed 



The State of Delaware 
Kent County, SS 
James Farrow one of the subscribing witnesses to the foregoing instrument of writing 
purporting to be the Last will and Testament of Jesse Dean late of Little Creek Hundred 
dec'd Comes before (unclear) Register for the Probate of wills and being sworn deposeth
and said that he saw the said Jesse Dean the Testator, sign the said Instrument and saw 
him also seal the same and heard him publish pronounce and declare the same as (unclear)
his last will & Testament that at the time of his so doing he was of souund & disposing
mind and memory and upward of 20 years of age. That the deponent attested and
subscribed his name as a witness to the said Instrument of writing at the Instance and 
in the presence of the said jesse Dean the Testator and in the presence of the
oath witness. 
(signed) james S. Farrow 
Subscribed & sworn this 7th day December 
1839
